definition: Supervising a student on its own rollouts using a teacher's distribution at those prefixes, which removes the train-inference mismatch of learning from a teacher corpus and gives dense token-level signal where an outcome reward gives one bit. Across 7 sources its objective and its ceiling are both under question. The objective is token agreement, and that has a named failure: a student can drive agreement to near-perfect by looping while the response as a whole is broken, so the metric is satisfied by degeneration rather than by learning -- with the two directional causes separately identified as student-excess tokens whose log-ratio corrections grow unbounded and student-deficit tokens no on-policy update ever reaches. The ceiling is the sharper finding. Measured from K=1 to K=1024, it raises average correctness at every budget while its pass@K advantage reverses at large budgets, a problem-level accounting finds more problems forgotten than learned with the retained set carrying the gain, and a perplexity analysis shows mass moving toward paths the base already supported -- so what transfers is sampling efficiency rather than capability. Four published variants reproduce the pattern and off-policy distillation, evaluated identically, does not. One further caution about effect sizes: one improvement's margin is 1.0 point where the student is close to the teacher, inside the spread of three other baselines, and 13.4 where it is far below -- and the strong-mismatch baseline is a model emitting 22K-token unterminated responses, so much of what is demonstrated there is repair of breakage.

evidence.note: Removes external supervision from on-policy self-distillation by building a pseudo-solution from the model's own majority vote and using it as privileged teacher context rather than as a scalar reward, then distilling only on the completions that disagree with it.
evidence.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision

evidence.note: Distributes hindsight supervision across the turns of an agent trajectory by comparing each turn's share of total revision magnitude against its share of eligible tokens, holding the average multiplier at one so the total supervision is fixed and only its allocation changes -- and isolates that allocation with a permutation control that keeps the multiplier values and scrambles which turn receives which.
evidence.title: Trajectory-Relative Hindsight Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

evidence.note: Gives the teacher in on-policy self-distillation access to each completed student rollout and its verified outcome, adapting it to preserve behaviour on successes and redirect failures toward verified success, while the student keeps a prefix-only interface it can actually deploy.
evidence.title: PAST: Privileged Adaptation from Complete Student Trajectories for On-Policy Self-Distillation

evidence.note: Replaces GRPO's z-score group normalisation with a temperature-scaled softmax over rewards, which keeps the induced prompt-difficulty weighting bounded as pass probability approaches one and turns the temperature into a dial between REINFORCE and maximum-likelihood weighting.
evidence.title: SoftmaxGRPO: Learning to Reason using Softmax Advantage Group Estimation

evidence.note: Gives the teacher branch of an on-policy self-distillation setup an abstract skill card -- a principle, when it applies, and the mistakes to avoid -- instead of the reference solution, so the privileged signal carries no answer and the gain lands on exactly the rollout groups where group-relative reward is algebraically silent.
evidence.title: Distill Skills into Weights, Not Prompts: Abstract Skills as Privileged Signals for On-Policy Self-Distillation

evidence.note: Identifies degenerate agreement -- students reaching near-perfect token agreement with a teacher by looping while the response as a whole is broken -- and replaces the agreement objective with two directional mismatch corrections, one bounding runaway excess tokens and one injecting teacher-preferred mass at positions the student almost never samples.
evidence.title: Mismatch Matters: On-Policy Distillation Beyond Token Agreement

evidence.note: Evaluates on-policy distillation across sampling budgets from 1 to 1024 and finds it consistently improves accuracy at small budgets while losing to the untrained base model at large ones, so what it transfers is sampling efficiency rather than capability -- and off-policy distillation, tested the same way, does expand the boundary.
evidence.title: Towards Understanding On-Policy Distillation through the Lens of Test-Time Scaling

name: on-policy distillation
